# `bank-line` commands

## `bank-line add`

Enter a waiting bank line in the books, run as you with the account's own command (check post or deposit post on a bank account, card-charge post or card-credit post on a card), so the entry is exactly the one you would type: the line's date and amount, your payee and account (or splits), class and memo (default the bank's text). No payee or account: refused, asking -- ask the person, never guess. A closed period refuses with the command's own code. Give `line`, or `lines` for several as one batch (undone together by `bank-line undo`); a batch is all or nothing. Reversing the import undoes it too. Example: {"line": "01J...", "payee": "Shell", "account": "Fuel"}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | bank-feed |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bank-line.add` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow bank-line add --line 01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BG --payee "Central Supply" --account "Office Supplies" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Enter the supplies purchase" --dry-run --json`

## `bank-line deposit`

Add more details: enter a waiting bank line of money in as a deposit of the customer payments and sales receipts waiting in Undeposited Funds that it banked, run as you with `deposit post` on the line's account and date, so the deposit is exactly the one you would type. A payment already deposited is refused by `deposit post`'s own code. `adjustment_account` enters a difference as one more row (other money received from a payee, or money kept back such as a bank fee) instead of refusing. The selection must come to the line exactly; otherwise it is refused showing the difference remaining (`details.difference`). The act is its own batch (`bank-line undo <batch_id>` takes it back) and is recorded on the line's import, so reversing the import takes it back too. Example: {"line": "01J...", "payments": ["01J...", "01J...", "01J..."]}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | bank-feed |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bank-line.deposit` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow bank-line deposit --line 01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BG --payments '["01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BH"]' --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Banked the Riverside checks" --dry-run --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "bank-line deposit", "input": {"line": "01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BG", "payments": ["01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BH"]}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `line` | `--line` | string | yes | no | — | A waiting line of money into a bank account.; pattern "^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$" |
| `payments` | `--payments` | array[string] | yes | no | — | The customer payments and sales receipts waiting in Undeposited Funds that this line banked (`deposit sources` lists them). They must add up to the line exactly, or name an `adjustment_account` for the difference. |
| `adjustment_account` | `--adjustment-account` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Enter the difference between the line and the payments as its own row of the deposit, instead of refusing: the line more than the payments, other money received, credited to this account (interest, a payment not yet entered...); the line less, money kept back from the deposit, debited here (a bank fee, cash back). Unsure? Ask the person; never guess. |
| `adjustment_payee` | `--adjustment-payee` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Who the other money came from (needed when the line is more than the payments; refused on money kept back). |
| `adjustment_payee_type` | `--adjustment-payee-type` | literal["customer", "vendor", "employee", "other_name"] \| null | no | yes | null | The list adjustment_payee is on; default customer. |
| `adjustment_memo` | `--adjustment-memo` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `adjustment_class_id` | `--adjustment-class-id` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The other money row's class (a cash-back row takes none, so it is refused there). |
| `memo` | `--memo` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The deposit's memo; default the bank's text. |

## `bank-line ignore`

Set a waiting bank line aside with a reason: already_entered, not_ours, duplicate (a possible_duplicate flag) or other. `bank-line unmatch` brings it back. Give `line`, or `lines` for several as one batch (undone together by `bank-line undo`); a batch is all or nothing. Reversing the import undoes it too. Example: {"line": "01J...", "ignore_reason": "duplicate"}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

## `bank-line match`

Match a waiting bank line to the entry it is, already in the books; the entry is not changed. Name the entry, or leave it out to take the line's one candidate; when several fit equally they are listed, never chosen. Amounts must agree exactly. Give `line`, or `lines` for several as one batch (undone together by `bank-line undo`); a batch is all or nothing. Reversing the import undoes it too. Example: {"line": "01J...", "entry": "01J..."}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

## `bank-line pay-bills`

Add more details: mark open bills paid from a waiting bank or card line of money out, run as you with `bill pay` from the line's account on its date, so the payment is exactly the one you would type. One line is one payment to one vendor; name `amount` per bill for a part payment. No method: refused, asking -- ask the person, never guess. The selection must come to the line exactly; otherwise it is refused showing the difference remaining (`details.difference`). The act is its own batch (`bank-line undo <batch_id>` takes it back) and is recorded on the line's import, so reversing the import takes it back too. Example: {"line": "01J...", "bills": [{"bill": "01J..."}], "method": "Bank Transfer"}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | bank-feed |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bank-line.pay-bills` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow bank-line pay-bills --line 01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BG --bills '[{"bill": "01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BH"}]' --method "Bank Transfer" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Paid the supplier online" --dry-run --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "bank-line pay-bills", "input": {"line": "01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BG", "bills": [{"bill": "01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BH"}], "method": "Bank Transfer"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `line` | `--line` | string | yes | no | — | A waiting line of money out of a bank or card account.; pattern "^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$" |
| `bills[].bill` | inside `--bills` JSON array | string | yes | no | — | An open bill (id or number).; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |

## `bank-line transfer`

Record a waiting bank line as a transfer between two of your accounts, as one entry: with its other end (`pair`, or the one proposed when exactly one fits both ways), both lines link to an existing transfer of that amount nearby, or to one posted with transfer post; with `to` and no line yet, the transfer is posted now and the other account's line matches it when imported; that line, arriving later, completes it (never a second transfer). Several fits are listed, never chosen. Example: {"line": "01J...", "pair": "01J..."}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | bank-feed |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bank-line.transfer` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow bank-line transfer --line 01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BG --to Savings --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Moved to savings" --dry-run --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "bank-line transfer", "input": {"line": "01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BG", "to": "Savings"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `line` | `--line` | string | yes | no | — | A waiting line.; pattern "^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$" |
| `pair` | `--pair` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The other end: a waiting line of the other account. |
| `to` | `--to` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The other account, when its line is not imported yet (a one-sided transfer). |
| `entry` | `--entry` | string \| null | no | yes | null | An existing entry moving the money between the two accounts. |
| `new` | `--new` | boolean | no | no | false | With to: post a new transfer even though one already posted from that account may be this line's other end (refused otherwise, naming it). |

## `bank-line undo`

Undo a bank-line batch (the batch_id of a --lines act) as one unit: delete the entries it made (with preserved history, by each family's own command) and return its lines to how they stood. Refused, naming each blocker, when a line was sorted again since or an entry was edited or used. --dry-run shows the plan. Example: {"batch": "01J..."}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | bank-feed |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bank-line.undo` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow bank-line undo 01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BJ --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Wrong account on the batch" --dry-run --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "bank-line undo", "input": {"batch": "01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BJ"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `batch` | `BATCH` | string | yes | no | — | The bank-sort batch (`batch_id` of a --lines act).; pattern "^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$" |
| `limit` | `--limit` | integer | no | no | 100 | Most created entries to delete in this call.; minimum 1; maximum 20000 |
| `fingerprint` | `--fingerprint` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The `fingerprint` a dry run returned; refused if anything changed since. |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |

| `--source-ref TEXT` | Identifier of the source that triggered the write. |
| `--interactive` | Prompt for input fields not supplied as arguments or options. |
| `--directive TEXT` | Standing-instruction code or id cited by the write. |
| `--idempotency-key TEXT` | Retry-safe key for this create command. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bank-line.undo`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |

| `Idempotency-Key` | optional | Retry-safe key for this create command |

### Output

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## `bank-line unmatch`

Return a bank line to waiting: undo its match or transfer link (the entry stays), or its ignore. A line entered as an entry is taken back with that entry (its delete or void) or the import's reversal; once that entry is gone (entry_gone), this releases the line. Give `line`, or `lines` for several as one batch (undone together by `bank-line undo`); a batch is all or nothing. Reversing the import undoes it too. Example: {"line": "01J..."}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | bank-feed |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bank-line.unmatch` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow bank-line unmatch --line 01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BG --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Wrong entry" --dry-run --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "bank-line unmatch", "input": {"line": "01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BG"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |

| `lines` | `--lines` | array[string] | no | no | [] | Several lines as one batch (kind bank-sort, undone together by `bank-line undo`); instead of `line`. |
